utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the absence of Judge Orie, the Tribunal, this Trial Chamber will be sitting according to Rule 15 bis. Could the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am a just checking if our videolink with Belgrade is working correctly. Yes, I can hear the witness. Mr. Groome, go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Before I continue my examination, I just want to inform the Chamber that the technical problem with respect to uploading the video that we ended with, 65 ter 6431, we are still in the progress of sorting that out, but we expect by the end of the first break that we will have done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Opacic. I would like to pick up where we ended yesterday. If you recall, I asked you what you meant when you said in a public speech: "We must kill such people on the spot." And you said the following: "Those people who betrayed the places where the weapons were, who gave them away, and they were the inhabitants there, also I don't know for what reason they disclosed the places where the weapons were being hidden, and they were telling UNPROFOR that. And I said that those people should have been killed. And to this very day, I stand by that, that every single one of those people should have been killed for weakening the combat strength of the Serbian people in the Krajina." Do you recall giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that and I stand by it, and I would repeat that again, today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd like to now ask you a few more questions with respect to this so that we fully understand your evidence. You said that the people who told UNPROFOR where Serb forces had hidden weapons should be killed on the spot. Am I correct that you are referring to the period immediately after a peace settlement had been reached and it had been agreed by both sides to the conflict that they would secure their weapons under the supervision and control of UNPROFOR peacekeepers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now at page 83 of yesterday's transcript, you said the following with respect to these weapons: "Then our army, which was the army of the Krajina at the time, had some weapons concealed, self-propelled weapons and things like that." The weapons that Serb forces had concealed was in violation of that peace agreement, was it not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for me that does not constitute a violation of the peace agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If it did not constitute a violation of the peace agreement, why was it considered necessary to conceal them from UNPROFOR peacekeepers?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely because we did not have confidence in them. You saw that there was an attack on Ravni Kotari and the UNPROFOR was protecting us while the Croatian army was attacking us, and our weapons were being under control and they would not release the weapons. And as for how they actually did protect us, well, that can be seen from what happened to us. Did the Croats respect the peace agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, let's confine our inquiry at this moment to the weapons themselves. Isn't the truth of this that you and other members of Serb forces conceal these weapons in violation of the peace agreement because you did not trust UNPROFOR peacekeepers to safe-guard Serbs? Isn't that the truth of this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not trust the peace forces. I did not trust them. Perhaps the authorities before did trust them, but actually we did not trust the UNPROFOR because we knew that they were partial.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the people who revealed the location of these weapons were simply people who wanted the peace agreement to be observed. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were citizens or inhabitants who had grudges against each other. So in order to get back at each other, they would give away that such and such a person was carrying a machine-gun or something like that. There was a case where somebody reported their neighbour because they did not want to harvest the wheat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The people you say should have been killed, what was their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It was your opinion in August of 1992, and remains the same today, that Serbs who took steps to ensure that there was compliance with the peace agreement should have been killed on the spot; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which agreement? These people have nothing to do with any agreement. These people did not sign any agreement. These were inhabitants of the villages, the different villages where these things were. What did they know about any agreements?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you're saying that the people that you wished to kill were not aware of the peace agreement that prevailed at the time and that this had nothing to do with the peace agreement. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, what you say, that I wanted to kill them, had I wanted to kill them I would have done so. I said they should have been killed. This is quite a different thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please explain to us what the difference is between those two statements.

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had I wanted to, I would have killed them. I believe that all those people who were betraying things and weakening the defence of Republika Srpska ought to have been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: By who?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who? Well, I don't know. I mean, I should have killed them. Well, there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would -- if you -- if you had had the opportunity to kill one of these people, would you have taken that opportunity?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew those people. I didn't kill them. I didn't want to kill them. They were just retches.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, as you can imagine over the course of this long trial, the Judges have heard the evidence of many witnesses. Some witnesses of one witness may appear to be in contradiction to the evidence of another witness. It is helpful in their assessment of each witness's credibility and reliability to know something about the background of witnesses. I want to spend the next several minutes asking you questions about your background for this purpose. You, yourself, are not on trial in this case. I am simply asking these questions so that we may learn more about you. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let me ask you some general questions and then I will ask you some specific questions with respect to information we were able to find out about your background. My first question to you is whether you have ever been convicted of a crime?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was in Loznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please tell us when?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in 2003 or 2002. I don't know. But the verdict was reached in 2008 or 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell us what crime you were convicted of?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was convicted because the person caught me and tried to strangle me in front of my own mother, and when I saw what it was I hit him with my fist, and the man fell and he hit his head on the sidewalk.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you -- what was the name of the man who you hit and who fell and hit his head?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think his last name is Maric. I don't remember his first name. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you present -- it sounds as if you believe that you were defending yourself. Did you present this defence during your trial?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the defence. But the Court was corrupt and I was unjustly sentenced, and there was an expert examination of my eyesight, and everybody said that I could not have been responsible for that. I could not have hit the person from 10 metres away. The proceedings were conducted for seven or eight years. I was acquitted. Then there was an appeal. Then the Court in Belgrade finally passed a sentence that I was guilty and I was sentenced to one year in prison and a fine of 100.000 dinars, and I never actually -- sentence was suspended, and I actually never paid because I never believed that I was actually guilty of the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But you were convicted for hitting a person from 10 metres away. That's your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The plaintiff said that I was running. I rushed up to him and hit him, but actually what happened was that he caught me. I was standing in front of a church with my mother - and this was in Loznica - and he grabbed me by the neck and started to strangle me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting my learned friend, Mr. Groome, but I think it's important for the transcript. As far as the sentence, it was not recorded correctly. If I can see correctly on page 12, the witness said -- if you permit me, actually, but I think he can repeat. He was sentenced to a prison sentence but then he added the kind of sentence that it was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was sentenced -- I received a one-year suspended sentence. It was actually 16 [as interpreted] months of imprisonment but then it was commuted to one year suspended and 100.000 for court costs, and so on and so forth. I didn't know, actually. I didn't even wish to read the verdict because it's a shame of our court in such a way, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you have provided an explanation. Is this what you wanted to hear, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you permit me, I don't want to waste time, again it has been recorded as "16 months" but actually it was 6 months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think that when we go over the transcript again this will be corrected. Mr. Groome, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, you have said that it's your intention not to pay the fine given you by the judge who heard this case and that you intend not to pay because you don't believe that the verdict was a correct one. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I believe that it is a shame on the part of the judge who sentenced me in such a way on the basis of all of the parameters that were there against me and all the witnesses who gave false testimony. All of his witnesses lied.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Have you ever been convicted of any other crime?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I was or not. I've never been sentenced for anything before until I came to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when you say "sentenced before," you're talking about this case that you've just described to us? That's the only time in your mind or to your knowledge that you have been convicted of a crime.

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know if I had any other misdemeanors and things, but until I came to Serbia there was nothing. The only thing was that Croatia sentenced me for non-existing crimes that they ascribed to me in Skabrnja. I was sentenced to 20 years. Actually, before that I was not subject to any kind of criminal punishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In addition to these two case, the Loznica case and the Croatian case, have you ever been the subject of a criminal investigation to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of any criminal investigations against me. No. Which crimes?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Have you ever used an alias, a name other than your own name?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never used any alias. I've always used my own name, except when I went to Belgium for surgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was after I was wounded on the 22nd of January in 1993. I went to Belgium and I think my passport was in the name of Goran Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who issued you that passport? What country was it issued from?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was given a passport. I don't know who issued it, but I was given the passport by Minister Jarcevic, who was the foreign minister of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina. I didn't even see the passport. This guy told me that my name is Goran Petrovic, and I didn't actually see any of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why were you issued an alias for a -- and a false passport to travel to Belgium under an assumed name?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For my personal security, because in the west there were Croat Ustasha people whom I knew from before with whom I worked, so this was in order for them not to recognise me. It was for my personal security.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that we take a look at 65 ter 6419. It's at tab 28 in the binder that the Registrar has in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, the document that you are going to be shown, and I will summarise its contents in detail because of the difficult you have -- or you may have in seeing it, it's a Croatian Ministry of Defence Security and Information Service Official Note on a preliminary interview of a Mr. Joseph Bepo Bajlo on the 2nd of June, 1993, in Zadar. Mr. Bajlo, you may recall, was a fellow patient at the same clinic you were in. And as you've just told us, the official note states that you stayed in an eye clinic under the name of Goran Petrovic. Sir, this is a Croatian intelligence document regarding information about your stay in the eye clinic. You've told us why you went there under an assumed name. Did you provide any other documentation indicating that you were Goran Petrovic, or was it simply the passport?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. All I had was on the basis of that passport, which was issued from -- by Bepo Bajlo from Zadar, and he came for that surgery as well from Zadar. And he also needed it for that surgery and we spoke together. But I don't know of any other documents, but I do know about the passport, and I know that when I returned to the Military Medical Hospital in Belgrade, all my medical documents that were sent to the VMA hospital were in the name of Goran Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You mentioned that you travelled with someone who also needed surgery, but the record did not catch the name that you said. Can I ask you to repeat the name of the person who you went -- who went with you for surgery?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The individual whom I mentioned didn't travel with me because he had come from Zadar in Croatia and I travelled from Serbia. Matic escorted me. Now, the individual who was called Beljo, to me an interpretation, he was Bepo "balija," and he was in that same eye clinic in Antwerp where I was. He also had an eye surgery. I knew the man from the time I worked as a policeman in Zadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now you confirmed the name that Mr. Beljo, as you say, says you were under, and you confirm his identity. Both of these items were mentioned in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that we have page 2 in the original --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Bajlo is his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Page 2 in the original at the bottom and page 3 of the translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This Official Note further states that you told Bajlo, that you personally told him that you belonged to the unit of 30 men under the command of Captain Dragan and that you did not agree with Martic and Babic, and that you even attacked Babic during his visit to Benkovac. Do you recall saying this to Mr. Bajlo?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bajlo was lying. I didn't exchange more than two words with him. We just exchanged hellos. That was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's your evidence that while he accurately reported other information about you, this particular piece of information is a lie?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a lie. That's true. I never discussed this issue with him, nor did we really talk about anything much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is there a reason that you can tell us why Mr. Baljo would lie about this one particular piece of information that you -- he provided?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a reason. I'm a Serb and he's a Croat. Actually, I was a Serb Chetnik to them. And of course he would accuse me of anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And he would accuse you of anything simply because he was a Croat and you were a Serb? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I want to now talk about another event that our investigations into you were able to find some information about, and it regards the death of a man killed in the Knin prison shortly before you made the speech that we listened to yesterday afternoon. In 1992 did you ever go to the prison in Knin?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever transfer captured Croatian soldiers or members of the HVO to the Knin prison?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had never had any contact with the HVO, ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it correct that there were combat operations in the area of Kupres during April 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of these operations. I was never present in the Kupres front. No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 6420. And that can be found in tab 28 in the binder in Belgrade. The document is a report from the Security and Information Service of the Croatian government, dated 26 November, 1993. The document was recovered from the Croatian state archives by an investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor on the 27th of November, 2000. The Prosecution request that the document itself not be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, the subject of this report before you relates to the killing of a man named Davor Tadic in the Knin prison. The information provided indicates that Mr. Tadic was approximately 25 years old in 1992 and he was from Kola near Tomislavgrad. Mr. Tadic was captured as an HVO member of the 10th to the 11th of April, 1992, during combat operations in Kupres and was transferred to Knin, to the Knin prison, with a group of prisoners. He was killed shortly afterward. This report names you personally as the perpetrator of this killing and ascribes that you are actively involved in martial arts and you comitted this murder by kicking and punching Mr. Tadic. Has this refreshed your recollection whether you have ever been to the Knin prison and ever participated in the killing of a man?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only accurate thing is that I was into martial arts. All the rest is a lie. I was never in the Knin prison and never killed anyone, nor was I ever present in the Kupres theater of war. All these are lies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was well known who the prison guards were. I never worked there and I never went to the Knin prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 6420 as an exhibit, and we'd ask that the document be placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Madam Registrar, can we have a number for the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6420 will receive number P3099, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P3099 is tendered under seal. I said "is admitted under seal."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, the next thing I'd like to deal with, I believe, is the incident in Loznica which you've described to us your version of events. I'd like to take a look at the version from the perspective of others involved in the case. In 1991 [sic] you were a member of the Association of Disabled War Veterans in Loznica; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which year is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise, I misspoke. In 2001.

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was Miladin Maric a member of this veterans' group?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Miladin Maric was the president of the invalid and war veterans, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you expelled from this group on the 6th of September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was, because I accused him of being a thief. He stole packages of aid that were intended for the war disabled. And it wasn't just I who complained. There were other war invalids who complained, too, but I was the only one expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And why were you singled out for expulsion if others made the same complaint?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were expelled at a later date. I was the first one to be expelled for drawing everyone's attention to his maladministration.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd like us to take a look at the stated reasons why you were expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And could I ask that we look at 65 ter Exhibit 6424 and that can be found in tab 33 in the binder in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, you will soon be shown a document that the Prosecution received from the Republic of Serbia pursuant to an official request for assistance. The document is a decision from the Executive Committee of the Association of Disabled War Veterans in Loznica, dated the 11th of September, 2001. The decision indicates the reasons that you were dismissed from the veterans' group. My first question to you is whether you were given a copy of the group's decision when it was entered?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Under the statement of --

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Under the statements of reasons for your dismissal, an event at the office of the association on 6 September, 2001, is described. Paragraph 2 of the section states: "Opacic did not accept the explanation given to him. But in a very inappropriate, rough, and insulting manner, he hurled curses and threats at the president of the association, cursing his communist mother and physically attacking him in front of several people." Do you acknowledge that you physically attacked the president of the association?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you accept or acknowledge that you used -- or, you cursed him and used the inappropriate language and threats in speaking with him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I told him was that he was a commie and a thief. I did not curse him. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution would tender 65 ter 6424 as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, under what exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6424 will receive number 3100, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Document P3100 is tendered -- is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Opacic, about a year later, on the 28th of August, 2002, did you go to a gathering of disabled war veterans at the church in Loznica?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is this not the day on which you assaulted a person who you've described and was convicted for crimes associated with that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I left that sorry association of disabled war veterans, the 28th of August is my Saint Patron's Day, and with my mother, my wife, and two daughters, I was on my way to the church for service. And this man, Miladin Maric, gathered a number of war veterans in order to stage a protest outside of the municipality building because their funds had been blocked by the municipal authorities on account of his maladministration.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat the last thing he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, the interpreter did not quite understand what you just said, the last portion of your sentence. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Miladin Maric had gathered the disabled war veterans in order to stage a protest. I, on the other hand, happened to pass by the area because I was on my way to the church, so I didn't intend to participate in this protest. So as my mother, my wife and two children and I happened to walk past this group of people, I asked my wife who they were and she said, They are the disabled war veterans who gathered there to stage a protest. At that point I said out loud that they were commies and frauds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that we take a look at 65 ter 6422. It's tab 31 in the binder in Belgrade. I'd ask if we can go to page 2 of the B/C/S original and English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Opacic, this is an arrest report connected with this event. It is filed by a police officer by the name of Zoran Opacic, and it was filed on the 9th of September, 2002. Was this report filed by your brother? Is this the Zoran Opacic that is your brother?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which Zoran Opacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The police officer who drafted this report.

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Authorised officials -- Zoran Opacic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear because of the overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The police official who filed this report, if you look at the very last page, Zoran Opacic. Is that the same Zoran Opacic who you have described as being your brother?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is an inspector in the Loznica police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is he --

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is not my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does he have any --

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are Opacic families in Loznica, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is he any relation to you that you know of?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I am going to read to you what -- how he described the event, based upon his initial assessment and interviews with people: "Around 0900 hours Goran Opacic, a disabled war veteran, suffering from severe vision impairment, came with his wife to the church with the intention of attending the service in the church. Since his vision is impaired he asked his wife, Zorica, what was happening there, and she said it was a rally of disabled persons. Then he asked where Miladin Maric, the president of the Loznica RBI, was. She told him where he was, and when he passed by Miladin, Goran -- when he passed by Miladin, Goran started hurling insults at him, calling him a crook and a thief, but as Miladin paid no attention to his insults, Goran went to the church entrance. When his wife went to buy candles, he was standing outside the entrance door, and then Radenko Maric, Miladin's son, who came to make footage of the protest of disabled war veterans, came to him and said that it was not the place or the time to argue with Miladin. Then Goran punched him in the head, so Radenko fell from the blow and his head against the monument." That is how the original police officer investigating this event reported it. Do you accept that he has accurately reported the events of that day?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He must have taken a statement from eye-witnesses there because he wasn't there. Well, I did say what happened. Radenko Maric caught me by the neck and started strangling me in front of my mother and outside the church, and that is the real truth. And as for what everybody else had to say, including this institution, they are lying.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could we now have on our screens 65 -- I'm sorry, 65 ter 6423, the first instance judgement regarding this assault on Radenko Maric. And that is at tab 32 in the binder below. Your Honours, recognising that the witness would be unable to read the document, can I suggest that we simply mark both 6422 and 6423 at this time for identification and that I postpone formally tendering them into evidence until the Chamber has had an opportunity to review the documents. The Defence have had the documents since yesterday. Perhaps they have already formed a view as to whether they will oppose their admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there an objection to the admission to this document, 65 ter 6422? Apparently not. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I just inquire as to whether it's just for impeachment purposes?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in that case, yes, it can be admitted, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, would you please give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6422 will receive number P3101, and document 6423 will receive number P301 -- P3102, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So P301 -- P3101 and P3102 are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask, as soon as it's convenient, that 65 ter 6421 be brought to our screens, and it is in tab 30 in the binder in Belgrade. This is a report sent to the State Security Service of Serbia, in particular the JSO. It is dated the 15th of March, 1999, but refers to earlier events.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, the next document that I would like to discuss with you is 65 ter 6421. Recognising your problems with vision, I am going to describe and quote parts of the report so we are able to discuss it. And the report concerns largely yourself and a person who you have given evidence about, Mr. Zoran Rajic. The report states, in part: "Rajic, Zoran, was engaged in criminal activities. He took tractors and tractor attachments away from the non-Serb residents and transported them onto the territory of Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Besides tractor equipment, he also 'transported' the TV sets, hi-fi equipment, video recorder." Is it true that Zoran Rajic was involved in transporting TV sets --

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, could you please wait for the Prosecutor to finish putting his question to you before answering. Otherwise, your answers cannot be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My question again: Is it true that Zoran Rajic was involved in the theft and transportation of stolen property, including tractors and electronic equipment, taken from non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a pure fabrication. Zoran Rajic didn't have need for any tractors or TV sets or whatever. It's a pure fabrication.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, so that you understand what the report is saying. It's not suggesting that Mr. Rajic was a farmer. It's suggesting that he was taking this property and selling it to gain money and to gain profit from these stolen goods. So I ask you again: Was Mr. Rajic involved in such activity?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, and I know for a fact that Zoran Rajic never did anything of the sort, ever, in his life. It's a big fat lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How are you so certain it is "a big fat lie"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because I know the man personally. We are on visiting terms and even have the bond of being --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter isn't sure if it's godfathers or witnesses of marriage, as the term is the same in the B/C/S, "kum."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is Zoran Rajic your "kum"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He is the "kum" of my brother, Milos.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The report continues and alleges that both you and your brothers were working with Rajic in this scheme: "The following were in business with Rajic: The brothers Opacic, Goran, Zoran, and Milos. They transported the goods in an official vehicle across the border (a Japanese-made pick-up truck). They engaged in the resale of cigarettes in this manner." Is this true?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see Zoran was never present in Ilok. You did mention Ilok, did you not? My brother Zoran was never with us in Ilok. It was my brother Milos and I who were there. This is not true. And I was never involved any sort of smuggling or reselling cigarettes or anything, nor did Zoran Rajic ever do anything of the sort. He didn't need to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I apologise, I didn't mention it was in Ilok, but that is, in fact, where it occurred. How did you know that the allegation referred to Ilok?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assumed because you said it was across the border and that was in that period. There is no other such period except that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You knew it was Ilok where these allegations arose because Ilok is near the border. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, because we are in Ilok and that is from that same period, so it must be that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't even mention the year or the period when this occurred. How do you know it's that period, the period you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I did not read to you any portion of the document that established what time-period it referred to. So my question is: How did you know the allegations -- or, why did you assume the allegations concerned the time-period that you personally were in Ilok?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assumed that because you mentioned the border and smuggling of cigarettes across the border and that's how or that's why, on the basis of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you explain the logic of that? It's not clear to me. The border is quite a long border and there are many towns on both sides of the border between Serbia and Croatia or Serbia and Bosnia. Can you walk us through the logic of how you knew it was in Ilok and referred to the time when you were there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's that period. I think that that's because that border between Serbia and Croatia is there and that we were smuggling cigarettes and things. That's alleged. But that was in that period, but that has nothing to do with anything. I mean, I heard these stories before, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The last line of the first paragraph suggests that Zoran Rajic was under pressure from you because he owed you a great deal of money: "Rajic, Zoran, owed big money to Opacic, Goran, and that Rajic was under the influence and under the pressure of Opacic." Is this true?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are just pure lies, nothing else. Rajic, under pressure, because he owed me money? Where does that come from? Who wrote that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's a report sent to the state security of Serbia, in particular, the JSO. The next paragraph goes on to describe how JSO members of the Poskok Detachment set aside their daily wages to help other members of the detachment having financial difficulties. Are you aware of a detachment of the JSO known as the Poskok Detachment? And that's P-o-s-k-o-k.

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in Ilok. I don't know what the name was, Poskok or something. But that's true, those people did help me. This is what I was saying before. But this was not in Ilok. It was on Tara.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is the Poskok Detachment the unit that you described yesterday that you were -- that your name was listed as a member when, in fact, you were not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And it's your evidence that the members of this unit sacrificed approximately one month of their salary each to give you 20.000 Deutschmarks so that you could purchase a home. That's your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my evidence and this took place in 1996/1997, when at the proposal of Zoran Rajic, when I was with them when we were on this endurance training, I was an advisor to Zoran Rajic about these preparations, so he suggested for them to give up one month's salary in my favour so that I could settle my housing problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The report was submitted by a person by the name of Zoran Gulic. Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution would tender 65 ter 6421 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, Madam Registrar, could we have the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6421 will receive number P3103, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P3103 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday Mr. -- I'd like to turn our attention now to the events in Skabrnja. Yesterday Mr. Bakrac asked you about events in Skabrnja, and you told us that although you intended to go and participate in that action, you decided before getting there to flee; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not run or flee. I withdrew.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think you said you took a car and left; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In --

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took my own -- actually, the people who were with me, all of them, we took -- may I just complete my thought, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I withdrew from Skabrnja, like I said yesterday. I withdrew because I saw that something was not quite right there and a few people withdrew. I turned around. I took my people and went from Biljane Donji to Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In summary, your evidence is the following: You were part of a reconnaissance group accompanied by tanks and APCs and was approaching Razovljeva Glava elevation outside the town of Skabrnja. When you came within 800 metres of the Razovljeva Glava --

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no it wasn't like that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, sir, please, can you make sure that you do not overlap with Mr. Prosecutor, otherwise your words cannot be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll break it down bit by bit so we can be sure where I may have understood your evidence incorrectly. You were part of a reconnaissance group that was ordered to go on a mission in the Skabrnja area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At least at the time you set off for this mission you were accompanied by at least one tank and some armoured personnel carriers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was accompanied by two tanks. There were no armoured personnel carriers there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the next part: This group approached the elevation known as Razovljeva Glava outside the town of Skabrnja; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you came within 800 metres of that elevation, the two tanks were ordered to return to the starting position and wait; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You considered the order to withdraw the tanks a betrayal and an attempt to get you and your men killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You said at transcript page 31 yesterday: "I was afraid that the army might set us a trap again with a view to having us killed during the action." Did you flee the scene because of cowardice or because you genuinely believed your superior officer was attempting to get you killed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which superior officer? Are you thinking of Zoran Lakic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: He's the person that you testified yesterday ordered you to engage in this operation; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. He was my superior officer. I did not run or escape, as it is written there. I withdrew. I pulled back. Secondly, I was never a coward. Had I been a coward I would never have been wounded in the eye but in the ass.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But you believe the withdrawal of the tanks was an attempt by Lakic to get you killed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lakic has nothing to do with that. This is the army, but Lakic was the commander of the Territorial Defence. This is the military command, the JNA. Zoran Lakic never had tanks under his command. Zoran Lakic was the commander of the Territorial Defence. He had nothing to do with that. We are talking about military security here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, what is the name of the person you believed was setting a trap for you in order to have you killed during this action?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ristic, Major Ristic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And why would Major Ristic --

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Ostojic, Milivoj Ostojic, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why would Major Ristic and Milivoj Ostojic -- what reason would they have for entrapping you and getting you killed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there must have been idealogical reasons involved; idealogical reasons because I accused them of being traitors and war profiteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what evidence do you have to support the fact that this was an effort to get you killed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as you can see, the first action on the 2nd of October, when we had the action in Nadin, they ordered the military police which was located 6 kilometres away from that conflict -- they ordered that military police, instead of coming to help us, to go to target practice in the range in Listici [phoen], and only at 5.00 after they were asked to come and help us, they came with two APCs to pull us out. So what else could one think except for that? The whole day we were stuck there, whereas it was only 6 kilometres involved which you can cover by car in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I -- sorry for interrupting, Mr. Groome, but I did promise the witness because of his difficulties that we will be having breaks every 75 minutes, so I'm just reminding everyone that perhaps this would be a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This would be convenient time if it's convenient for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will have a break. But just before the break, Mr. Groome, there is a document, a 65 ter document that you wanted to show about a hospital. I think it was 65 ter 649. You haven't tendered it. Or perhaps we can do it after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I will investigate that, Your Honour, and deal with it first thing when we get back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will have a break and we will resume at a quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We resume. Yes, Mr. Groome. I asked you about -- I asked you about 65 ter document 6149. [In English] 6419.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I thank the Chamber for bringing my failure to tender that document to my attention. It is something that the Prosecution tenders into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, then document 6419 is admitted. Can we have a numbers, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6419 will receive number P3104, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The video-clip that we saw yesterday, the video number 6431, was it -- it was finally provided to the Registrar. Do you want it admitted as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It has been prepared and transmitted to it Registrar. So the Prosecution at this time would formally tender 6431.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that there are no objections to the admission of the document. So video number 6431 will be admitted. Can we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document video 6431 will receive P3105, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Groome, you may continue your cross-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Opacic, I'd like to now turn to a different topic, the events in Skabrnja. You indicated earlier today that you know that you have been convicted for crimes perpetrated against the civilian population of Skabrnja; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that we have on our screens 65 ter 6415. And that can be found in tab 24 in the binder in Belgrade. This is a first instance judgement of a trial associated with those events. And the judgement is dated the 7th of July, 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In this judgement, Mr. Opacic, Judge Milan Petricic sentenced you to 20 years incarceration after finding you did the following. And I am reading from e-court pages 4 in the original and 4 in the English: "They entered the village of Skabrnja, the exclusively Croat populated region, in several groups. Headed by the accused Goran Opacic, Bosko Drazic." The judgement continues a few lines later referring to you and your men: "They shell the village without prior selection of military targets. After which, they forcefully pulled out from cellars and other shelters civilians and noncombatant locals, mainly women and the elderly, and children as well, who did not stage any resistance nor posed any threat to the aggressor. Then they killed at least 44 persons from firearms at close range or with blunt objects on the head and molested and massacred few persons before they killed them." Judge Petricic finds that these acts constituted international crimes. My question to you is simply: Were you aware of the crimes perpetrated in Skabrnja?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that, no. I did not participate in that and I did not see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you know any of the men present in Skabrnja?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which men, the ones who were in Skabrnja?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did any of the men who were part of your unit, do you know whether any of them were in the town of Skabrnja?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none did. None were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you learn about the crimes comitted in Skabrnja?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard the stories later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When did you first hear what you describe as stories?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I know that there were --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us or summarise the stories that you heard a couple of days later?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What can I say? These were just stories, that usually people retell around town that the -- this Lieutenant Stevanovic was killed by a rifle and that there was a clash they had between those military forces and the Croatian forces. This is all that I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this moment I am more interested in whether you heard anything about the crimes comitted against the civilians of the town, mostly elderly people?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I did not hear of any crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that the first time you heard anything about these crimes is when I have -- when I just read a description of them a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Read about the crimes? I didn't have the sentence, though, the verdict. But I did see it in newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: One of the men found guilty, Jovan Badzoka, was before the court. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's from my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Listen to how Judge Petricic summarised part of his evidence. When Judge Petricic uses the pronoun "he," it is a reference to Badzoka: "He heard about the attack and suffering of Skabrnja several days after the event had occurred. He was at his home but the information were not extensive. There were only talks that many people were killed and that the JNA did it and that Goran Opacic was there." He says that he learned immediately after the attack that you were there. Do you still deny that you were present in Skabrnja?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a staged trial. I mean, you can see that. It's so evident.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is there any reason why Badzoka would have a reason to fabricate your presence in Skabrnja?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of fear of the Croats. Anybody who went there or who returned for any kind of killing or anybody who was killed, this was always something that they ascribed to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I was a former policeman. I fought in the police. I fought against Croats with all my might. I fought against them. And this is a staged trial by the Croats against me. They had no other reasons for me to commit any crimes. But on the basis of lies and statements of those people who were there, they drafted the charges. It's a staged trial. I never participated in any crimes. I wasn't even there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name of Slobodan Coso?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Mirko Coso. I don't know Slobodan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How do you know Mirko Coso?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Mirko Coso from Jagodnja Gornja.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was he a member of your unit during this period?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: One of the witnesses in that trial, Marijan Pesut, that's P-e-s-u-t, recounted statements made by one of the direct perpetrators of the crime, a Slobodan Coso, who identified himself as a member of the Goran Opacic group. Judge Petricic summarised Pesut's evidence: "He remembers the words of Slobodan Coso, that Goran Opacic was the cruelest and that very few people would survive the passage of his unit." The judgement goes on to describe in detail the crimes comitted upon the civilians of Skabrnja, the summary executions of elderly people with bullets to the heads, the international running over of a woman with a tank, and made the following finding: "In respect to accused Goran Opacic, Bosko Drazic, Zoran Jankovic, it was established that they were not only the executors of the crime but also ordered the above-crime."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that can be found at B/C/S e-court page 41 and English 37.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, is it not a fact that not only were you were a direct participant in the crime but that you ordered some of the crimes perpetrated upon the civilians of Skabrnja?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 6415. It is the first instance judgement. It was provided to the Office of the Prosecutor by the public prosecutors office of Croatia on September 28, 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I am just wondering what the probative value is of this report. My learned friend's cross-examined the witness on an issue of credibility, suggesting he was there. The witness has denied it. He's put the judgement finding to him. The witness has denied being there. That, in our submission, should be the end of it. We don't need a judgement and the judgement doesn't take the matter any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the judgement actually does take it much further and it describes in great detail this individual's participation in the crimes, and the Chamber really, in the Prosecution's submission, needs to have the judgement before it so it can properly assess what this person, what Mr. Opacic says now about the events in this -- this crime and what the findings were of the first instance judge -- the first instance court.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If it is just for impeachment then I will withdraw the objection, but if it's more than that, then I maintain the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's for impeachment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Document number -- I can't remember any more.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6415 will receive number P3106, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. So document 3016 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd now ask that we look at 65 ter 6416. That is in tab 25 of the binder in Belgrade. This is a second instance judgement entered on the 16th of June, 1998, by members of the Croatian supreme court, Judge Milan Gudelj presiding; and that's G-u-d-e-l-j.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, your case was appealed to the Supreme Court of Croatia. The judgement states that you were represented by a lawyer by the name of Filip Brdar, B-r-d-a-r. Do you confirm that he represented you in this appeal?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never appealed against that judgement before the Croatian court, nor do I know this man, Brdar. He is a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The Supreme Court summarised its finding as follows: "All indicted persons are responsible for committing the crime together and former mentioned three indicted persons for commanding as well." That's at B/C/S page 5 and English e-court page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution would tender 65 ter 6416. It was received from the Zadar police administration on the 29th of September, 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Same position, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I imagine it's the same as well for Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Document number 6416 is admitted into evidence. Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6416 will receive number P3107, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I will repeat, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- document 6416 will receive number P3107, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There must be a mistake again in the number. P3107; is that right? Thank you very much. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the record still needs a bit of correction. I think it's P3107.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I will repeat one more time. And make sure there is no interpretation going on over what I am speaking. So I wait. Okay. So document 6416 will receive number P3107.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we have got it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Chamber may also be assisted with assessing this particular witness's evidence by Exhibits P1206 and P1207. These are interviews of two participants in the attack in Skabrnja conducted by military intelligence and describes some of the crimes in greater detail. I would like to focus on another military report, and that is P1208. I'd ask that that be brought to our screens. It can be found in tab 8 in the binder in Belgrade. This is a report of Major Branislav Ristic on 27 November, 1991, shortly after the crimes in Skabrnja.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Opacic, Major Branislav Ristic, was given the task of collecting information about the crimes in Skabrnja. The Chamber has before -- before it his notes of two interviews with participants in the attack on the village. In P1208 we have his report which includes information from a source he identifies as IS. The report states that you told IS that you were present in Skabrnja and that you blamed some of the crimes on a volunteer Chetnik group called Jaro-Jare. Do you deny the veracity of this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do deny it. I never said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know a group called Jaro Jare?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was never one such group, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The report goes on to recount your own very description of seeing an old man running away and then seeing an active duty soldier fire a hand-held rocket into the old man's back. The report states: "Goran Opacic said that he had never seen a more terrible sight in his life because the old man was blown to pieces, with just a leg remaining nearby." Do you deny that you said that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Groome, that is not the document that we have on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I apologise, Your Honour, I should have indicated that it was page 5 of that document. If I could ask that we go to that. I think we can see it now in the middle paragraph on that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, when I asked you earlier today about who it was that you thought would set you up and try to have you killed, I believe you said it was a Major Ristic was one of these persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Milivoj Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is -- this report is authored by a Major Branislav Ristic. Is this the person who you believed wanted to have you killed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now in this report Major Ristic doesn't accuse you of any wrong-doing. He simply reports what another informant told him you said. Is there any reason that you can think of that Major Ristic would want to attribute to you as having eye-witnessed a crime but not accuse you of actually committing that crime?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course he wanted to shift the blame onto someone, so he ascribed it to me because he was responsible for the crimes comitted in Skabrnja. Well, the commander of the military police unit that was present there was his security officer, and now I, who wasn't there at all, am supposed to take the blame for it; whereas, he, who was there in command of it all, should be cleared.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am finished with this report. And I would also refer the Chamber to P1209. It is also a report with respect to this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I would like the change the subject now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I would ask that we bring P428 to the screen, and it can be found in tab 2 of the binder in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And sir, keeping in mind your evidence that you had no employment with the Serbian DB, I want to go over a number of documents with you and explore whether or not that is true. Did you attend an award ceremony on security service day of the RSK in which you received a plaque?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never attended that meeting, nor was I given any sort of award while I was in the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If we take a look at this document, this is a list of individuals who received recognition on the occasion of security service day of the RSK. Your name appears as the 21st individual on this list. Would the fact that your name appears on a list of people receiving recognition refresh your recollection as to whether you were ever honoured in this way?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I am seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you ever a member of the RSK State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The list indicates that plaques were being awarded due to demonstrated bravery, self-sacrifice, or exceptional contribution to the successful operation of the internal affairs service. Do you know why you would have been -- why your name would appear on such a list?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. I was never on good terms with him.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name of the person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When was this awarded? What was the time-period?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let me first ask you to -- the interpreter did not catch the name that you mentioned, the person you were not on good terms with. Can you first tell us that, and then we can discuss when this might have been.

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mile Martic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And with respect to the date, it's unclear exactly what year, although it is clear that it occurred on the 5th of July. Now, were any of your brothers ever members of the RSK State Security Service or the Krajina DB?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Number 28 on this list indicates a plaque was awarded to the Benkovac SDB Detachment. Could you please tell us what detachment this refers to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That must have been the detachment headed by Aco Draca. He was there. He was the head of state security in Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Captain Dragan is listed immediately above your name at number 20. Was he present to receive this award, if you know?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present there. I know nothing about this event. I don't know who received awards.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I am finished with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Opacic, yesterday you said your brother, Milos, was in the Guards Brigade in Belgrade and not in Golubic with you. My question to you today is: Is it possible he was in Golubic during a period when you were not there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he definitely was not. He came in 1992, in early 1992, from the army. He was in the Guards Brigade in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that P2824 be brought to our screens, and it's tab 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to show you a document from your brother Milos's state security personnel file --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you for that reminder. Your Honour, perhaps out of an abundance of caution -- I don't think ultimately my questions will trigger a sensitivity, but perhaps in an abundance of caution if we could move provisionally into private session -- that be sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I want to correct what I just said. 65 ter 2D250 is on the Simatovic exhibit list. It is not a document that they, themselves, found in their investigations. In this letter sent by Mr. Rajic to Mr. Simatovic, he recommends eight men be given command responsibilities in the Poskok Detachment. We obtained this document -- the Office of the Prosecutor obtained this document from your very own personnel file provided by the government of Serbia, a file from the archives of the State Security Service. The first person on the list is your brother, Milos Opacic, detachment commander. Do you deny that your brother was the detachment commander of the Poskok Detachment of the JSO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, just before you answer, Mr. Bakrac would like to say something. Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do believe that we need to treat this witness more fairly than we do others in that he cannot possibly see the document before his eyes. Can Mr. Groome please let the witness know that the title is a proposal for the command cadre of the detachment, whereas Mr. Groome put it to him in the way that these -- this was already done or that they were commanders. So I think we should be more careful where this witness is concerned when we put questions to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're absolutely right, Mr. Bakrac. Mr. Groome, can you describe the document to the witness a little bit more in detail since he cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Bakrac is, indeed, correct. I will literally read the heading of this letter on state security stationery. Title of document: "Recommendation to Establish Commanding Personnel in the Poskok Detachment." Underneath the title, there are listed eight different people, each being recommended for a somewhat different position. I read down the names: "1. Milos Opacic. "2. Dusko Maricic. "3. Nikola Simic. "4. Goran Opacic, advisor for military affairs and sports activities. "Gavrilo Tutus. "Rajko Zezelj. "Jovo Mirkovic." And last: "Stevan Tutus." It is signed by Zoran Rajic and addressed to Mr. Simatovic. And, again, this came from a personnel file bearing your name in the State Security Service. So my first question to you is, again: Were you aware that your close friend, Zoran Rajic, had recommended to Mr. Simatovic that your brother, Milos, be made the detachment commander? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is when we were on Tara. I didn't know that he sent that letter, but I know that there was a proposal for my brother to be the commander for those services of Poskok because I was also proposed for physical training and preparations. It was 1996/1997, during the time that we were in Tara.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation as to how you, a person who has testified under oath, never had an employment relationship or was never working for the Serbian DB, has a personnel file in their archives?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I have a personnel file in their archives or not, but I was never a member. The only thing is if the connection is there because I worked there as Rajic's assistant for physical training. That could be the only connection. That's one thing. But I was never in that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In your last answer there is a reference to the few days that you spent in helping Mr. Rajic develop a plan for the physical conditioning of recruits. Is that what you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I am saying. Yes. That's the period when we were in Tara.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday you told us that the first time you actually spoke with Franko Simatovic was in a celebration at the Kula centre in 1997, and the first time you met Mr. Stanisic was --

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the first time you met Mr. Stanisic was at the same ceremony. Do you recall giving that evidence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you said that your first encounter with Mr. Stanisic was when he gave you a gift during that ceremony; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: As you know, we have a video of the celebration and can clearly see you there. In concluding my examination of you, I am going to play three specific portions that are relevant to you personally. Could I ask you to do your best to view the video but also to listen to the video. To orient you, the first portion of the video that I will play depicts introductions of a number of individuals, including yourself. You and the other men are being introduced to President Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this time I would ask Mr. Laugel to please play an excerpt of Exhibit P61. The time code -- I'm sorry, this excerpt is uploaded as 65 ter 58 -- the time code -- please disregard the reference to the 65 ter number. It's P61 and the time code from the original exhibit is 9 minutes, 2 seconds to 10 minutes, 2 seconds. May I ask that that be played now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "ZI: Mr. President, veterans of the Special Operations Unit of the Republic of Serbia State Security are lined up for inspection. Colonel Zika Ivanovic reporting! "SM: Hello, Ivanovic. "ZI: Mr. President, allow me to introduce the unit's veteran officers. "Mr. President, Colonel Radojica Bozovic! "SM: Hello Bozovic. I read those reports of yours. "RB: Thank you. God forbid there should be more of them, but should there be, I'm here. "ZI: Colonel Dusan Orlovic. "SM: Pleased to meet you. "DO: Likewise, comrade President. "ZI: Colonel Vasilje Mijovic! SM: Pleased to meet you. "ZI: Colonel Goran Opacic. "SM: Hello."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Groome, if is the same footage was shown to the witness that we saw, I am sure that he couldn't see much. He could hear, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I will explore that with him, Your Honour, to see if there is anything we can do to make sure that he has a full and fair opportunity to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, were you able to view any of that video or did you recognise the introductions that were made, including the introduction of yourself?

utterances.speaker: GORAN OPACIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't need to even look at it. I already know it. I told you yesterday that I was invited by Zoran Rajic to attend the anniversary celebration of the unit, and when we got there, I've given a uniform. We were introduced there has military war veterans, but I was never in that unit.
